Graduate Programs in Computer Science
At a Glance
Degrees: Master of Science (MS), with dual degree options available, or PhD
Format: In person, Waltham/Boston area
Master's Program Length: MS: 1.5 years, 9 courses (36 credits) for students with a CS undergrad degree; 2 years, 12 courses (48 credits) for non-CS majors
Admissions Deadlines: ​MS (fall): Jan. 15, March 1, April 15, then rolling until May 15 or until the cohort is full; MS (spring): Oct 15 (priority), Nov. 15 (final); PhD: Jan. 15
Funding: The majority of our master’s students receive some form of scholarship. Funding for PhD students includes a competitive fellowship, a full-tuition scholarship, and health insurance benefits for five years.
School: School of Science, Engineering and Technology
Learn More
Loading...
The Computer Science program at Brandeis provides students with strong foundations in three fundamental areas: designing and building software, developing effective ways to solve computing problems and devising new and better ways of using computers to address challenges.
Degree Options
Master of Science (MS) in Computer Science
Master of Science (MS) in Computer Science for Non-Majors
PhD in Computer Science
With an option to specialize in Quantitative Biology
Dual Degree Option
Combined BA/MS or BS/MS
Computer Science Curriculum
Students in Brandeis' graduate computer science program study the fundamental concepts underlying the development and use of computing systems. The curriculum includes computational complexity and information theory, the design and analysis of serial and parallel algorithms, and the development of programming languages, systems, and artificial intelligence.
PhD students may also participate in the Quantitative Biology Program where they will receive a PhD degree in Computer Science with an additional specialization in quantitative biology. Related research areas are machine learning, bioinformatics and biomedical informatics.
Computer Science Curriculum
Computer Science Career Paths and Outcomes
Brandeis computer science graduates have successfully launched into exciting careers at top companies around the country in fields ranging from Internet backbone to computer gaming. While the most frequent job title is "Software Developer," they work on a wide breadth of challenging problems. Companies include Akamai, Amazon, Blizzard Entertainment, Bloomberg, Commvault, EMC, Facebook, Google, Kaon Interactive, Tripadvisor and Vertica.
Students have the opportunity to engage in a wide variety of networking opportunities including the annual Computer Science job fair, smaller industry receptions targeting specific industries and recruiting visits from Google, Yelp and others. Our faculty industry liaison also provides individual consultations and resume reviews.

Master's Students
The majority of our master’s students will receive some form of scholarship. Brandeis offers several merit and need-based scholarships. Enrolled students may be offered paid course assistantships in some programs.
Doctoral Students
Funding includes a competitive fellowship, a full-tuition scholarship, and health insurance benefits for five years.
